turns.replyText:
I've been disappointed by similar products before, so quality really matters to me.

I hear you, and that makes a lot of sense. When you’ve been let down before, it’s hard to trust the next purchase.

A quick bit of context that may help: At Heirloom, all our roses are own-root (not grafted), grown at our nurseries in Oregon, virus-free, and shipped as actively growing 1-gallon plants in soil. We defoliate them before shipping so they travel well, but they’re fully rooted, not bare root. Our perennials and bulbs also go through careful quality checks, and everything is covered by our guarantees (1 year for roses, 90 days for perennials, and a failure-to-bloom guarantee for bulbs).

To make sure we choose something that truly fits what you need, can you tell me:

Are you looking for a rose, a different perennial (like lavender, hydrangea, etc.), or bulbs?
What specifically disappointed you with similar products before (weak plants, poor blooming, wrong color, disease issues, shipping quality, something else)?
Do you know your hardiness zone or city/state so I only suggest plants that will thrive where you are?

Once I know those three things, I can narrow it down to a few high-quality options that match exactly what you’re looking for.
